messages.subject: Replicated mapping population analysis in R/qtl2
messages.subject_clean: Replicated mapping population analysis in R/qtl2
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl et al.
I have a ril mapping population that was grown under two experimental treatments - all individuals in the population are grown in both environments.
I want to analyze this data in a mixed-effects model in R/qtl2 to assess QTL*Treatment interactions. This way, the same RIL in different environments will have a kinship = 1 and won't incorrectly affect the degrees of freedom.

Do you have any advice about how to set up the R/qtl2 objects to conduct this analysis?
As of now, I have the genotype matrix and a wide phenotype matrix (with one column for each experimental treatment). My thought is that I should melt the phenotype matrix so that there is one phenotype column and a corresponding treatment covariate. Then stack copies of the genotype matrix on each other to match the phenotype matrix.

Is there a better / simpler way to accomplish this analysis?
Thanks,
John

John Lovell
University of Texas at Austin

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Replicated mapping population analysis in R/qtl2
messages.body_plain:
I'd recommend sticking with R/qtl at present. Since you have two treatments, you can take the difference of the phenotype between the two treatments and map that as a trait; QTL that are identified are indicated to have different effects in the two treatments: QTL x treatment interaction.

karl

messages.subject: MAGIC population in R/qtl2
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl et al.
I am trying to construct the requisite matrices and control file to read the arabidopsis MAGIC population (http://mus.well.ox.ac.uk/magic/) into R/qtl2. The population has 19 parents and is inbred.

I am currently trying to read in using crosstype = "do", which I don't think is appropriate: "error: length(alleles) [19] != expected number [8]".

The population and parents are genotyped 0/2 (reference or alternative homozygote). Can R/qtl2 handle this type of data? If not, would it help to generate haplotypes so that each MAGIC line has one of 19 possible founder genotypes for each marker?
Thanks,
John

John Lovell
UT Austin

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] MAGIC population in R/qtl2
messages.body_plain:
R/qtl2 can't currently handle these 19-way MAGIC lines.
And I don't yet have an easy way to deal with haplotype calls.

R/qtl2 is not-quite-ready-for-prime-time.

I've added it to my to do list, and I hope to work on it this fall.

Regards,
karl

For an intercross, I'd be wanting at least 100-150 individuals.

For scantwo, there are 9 possible 2-locus genotypes, and 4 of them have frequency 1/16. And you start running into problems when some of those 2-locus genotypes aren't observed.

karl

messages.subject: Re: "mqmplot.multitrait" plots
messages.body_plain:
Dear Yusuf,

The colors are chosen from the rainbow scale in the order in which the phenotypes appear in the result object.
An example:

data(multitrait)
multitrait <- fill.geno(multitrait)
result <- mqmscan(multitrait, pheno.col=1:4)

# Names of the phenotypes in the result
phenoN <- unlist(lapply(result, function(x){ return(colnames(x)[3])} ))

# Make the plot, and add the legend
mqmplot.multitrait(result, "lines")
legend("topleft", phenoN, lwd = 1, col=rainbow(length(phenoN)))

Hope this helps,
Danny Arends

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Genetic Map Construction
messages.body_plain:
I wouldn't use the term "inappropriate".

Small values of min.lod will result in markers being placed in the same linkage group when they're not really linked.

Large values of min.lod will result in linkage groups being in multiple pieces.

The values to choose depend on the type of cross, the sample size, the number of markers, and the number of chromosomes. It's hard to say in advance what to use.

karl

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] run est.map for different chromosomes and combine the results
messages.body_plain:
I think I had suggested ordering the markers on each chromosome, one chromosome at a time.
And I would do this not by subsetting the cross, but by using the 'chr' argument in orderMarkers and est.map.

For calc.genoprob and scanone, I would work with the full set of chromosomes together.

While you can subset a cross by chromosome, I don't think there's an easy way to get them back together.
I would read in the full cross data and then re-order the markers as you'd determined them, but keep all chromosomes together.
